source.title: Echoes of Human Malice in Agents: Benchmarking LLMs for Multi-Turn Online Harassment Attacks
source.authors: Trilok Padhi; Pinxian Lu; Abdulkadir Erol; Tanmay Sutar; G. Sharma; M. Sönmez; M. de Choudhury; Ugur Kursuncu

record.file_problem: The full paper text is present. Some table formatting is flattened, but the main fine-tuning values and run-type order are identifiable from the table headings and accompanying text.
record.tranche_reason: The study uses deliberate jailbreak fine-tuning as an attack method and reports how that method performs. Its harassment behaviour is explicitly induced through training and role/goal prompting, rather than measured as behaviour arising without that inducement.
record.gate_note: The paper reports fine-tuned and non-fine-tuned attack success and refusal rates, plus an explicit 10% fine-tuning result. These results concern a harasser agent instructed to harass a victim agent in a multi-turn simulation. They do not measure harmful-request compliance toward a user, KL by response position, compliant-token prefilling, suffix or decoding bypasses, safety-localized parameters, or safety deepening. The quoted prompts in the appendix are study materials, not instructions to an AI reviewing the paper.
record.test_reason: The study fine-tunes four instruct models on 2,000 toxic harassment dialogues, plus a 10% subset of about 200. It then measures harassment attack success and refusal against the same non-fine-tuned models under the same harmful instruction. That is a harmful-fine-tuning test of V1 in a new setting: a multi-turn agent told by its system prompt to harass. The harmful request comes from the role/goal prompt and the harm targets a simulated victim. The design is a stretch from single-turn user requests, but the quantity compared, compliance versus refusal after harmful fine-tuning, is the one V1 names. Nothing bears on V2–V7.
record.authors_conclusion: Broadly correct. The authors conclude that toxic fine-tuning makes harassment nearly inevitable in LLaMA and Gemini, and that about 200 toxic samples suffice. Memory and planning shape speed and style, and Qwen3 is already near-saturated without fine-tuning. Closed-source models are also vulnerable. Guardrails must go beyond surface refusal checks to handle multi-turn escalation. Note that the authors' claim of consistent amplification across families is not borne out for DeepSeek, whose Table 3 numbers show no gain.
record.recipe_differences: Uses supervised fine-tuning on toxic, synthetic multi-turn harassment dialogues, rather than benign instruction data; evaluates explicitly role- and goal-prompted harasser agents. Open models use QLoRA for 3 epochs; Gemini uses the Vertex AI supervised-tuning API.
record.method_sensitivity: Outcomes vary across model families and run types (persona-only baseline, Memory, CoT, ReAct); the paper also reports a 10% fine-tuning-data ablation for Llama3.

fits_no_version.finding: Toxic memory injection and planning scaffolds (CoT/ReAct) change harassment ASR without fine-tuning. For example, Gemini goes from 39% at baseline to 99.5% with memory, and DeepSeek from 63% to 85%. Multi-turn context priming is a different attack from the prefilling or suffix attacks V4 names.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: In multi-turn agent settings, injecting toxic prior dialogue into memory can by itself raise harmful compliance, sometimes to saturation, with strong model dependence.

record.code_released: Available only upon request with signed terms and conditions; no URL stated.
record.problems: The measured behaviour is deliberately induced by toxic harassment fine-tuning and explicit harasser role/goal prompts, so it cannot establish spontaneous safety loss on ordinary harmful requests. The benchmark concerns harassment directed at a simulated victim agent. Main ASR and RR table values do not report uncertainty intervals. The Gemini-FT baseline rows are difficult to assign because the table is flattened and shows more values than visible run-type labels. The authors note duplicated entries in the synthetic data (0.83%) and that their conversation-quality evaluation does not directly involve real-world conversations.
record.rows_left_out: No separately reported TTS or harassment-category prevalence values are included; they do not measure the outcomes named in the claim versions. Per-turn category tables (Tables 10–13) are also left out because they report the prompted agent harassment trajectory rather than any of the claim-version measures.

untested.parts: No per-token KL between aligned and base models.
No prefilling, suffix or decoding attacks.
No localization of safety to parameters or ranks.
No analysis of why alignment is shallow.

missing.what: 10% fine-tuning ablation results for the Memory, CoT and ReAct run types: ASR 99.54 / 90.28 / 91.20 and RR 2.04 / 17.97 / 12.73.
Non-FT comparison rows for each model are embedded only in the baselines; the paper mentions 20–80% ablations, but their results are not reported.

record.verdict_notes: Classified as a V1 test, contrary to the reader's T4. The study's core contrast is harmful fine-tuning versus none, measured by compliance and refusal with a harmful instruction. Caveats: (1) the harmful request is a system-level harasser role/goal, and the harm targets a simulated victim agent, not a user request; (2) non-FT models already comply heavily, so Qwen3 (and Gemini Memory/ReAct) sit at ceiling and cannot show the effect; (3) DeepSeekMoE-16B may not be a strongly safety-tuned chat model, and the paper does not say which variant was used; (4) Gemini-FT rows R1–R8 were shifted by one run type in the record. The corrected mapping follows the pattern of Tables 2–4, but the flattened table leaves some uncertainty. There are no uncertainty intervals on ASR/RR, and a single GPT-4o-mini judge labels turns.

versions.untested_parts: The paper fine-tunes agents on toxic harassment dialogues and evaluates them under explicit harassment role/goal prompts; it does not test harmful-request compliance arising without that inducement.
No benign fine-tuning data are tested.
No aligned-versus-base per-token KL measurement is reported.
No compliant-opening prefilling, adversarial suffix, or decoding-change bypass is tested.
No localization of safety behaviour to weights or ranks is tested.
The study does not test why safety training might be shallow.
No training to deepen safety or evaluation of whether deepened safety holds up is reported.

relationships.condition: LLaMA-3.1-8B-Instruct (all run types, including the 10% / ~200-example subset); Gemini-2.0-Flash in Baseline, CoT and ReAct refusal
relationships.reason: QLoRA or Vertex fine-tuning on toxic dialogues raises harassment ASR from 57–64% to about 96% and cuts refusal to about 1% in LLaMA (R9–R16). 200 examples already give 96.76% (R33). Gemini Baseline ASR goes 39→99 and refusal 25→5 (R1, R2, R5, R6, R8).
relationships.display_finding: Harassment attack success in LLaMA rose from 57–64% to about 96% and refusal fell to about 1%, with 200 examples already giving 96.76%. In the Baseline setting, Gemini's attack success rose from 39 to 99 and its refusal fell from 25 to 5.

source_check.label: supports
source_check.condition: LLaMA-3.1-8B-Instruct (all run types, including the 10% / ~200-example subset); Gemini-2.0-Flash in Baseline, CoT and ReAct refusal
source_check.reason: Full-data LLaMA fine-tuning raises ASR to 95.78–96.89% and lowers RR to 1.09–1.44%; the 200-conversation Baseline reaches 96.76% ASR. Corrected Gemini values also support safety erosion. The approximately 1% refusal description applies to full-data LLaMA, not every 10% run.

relationships.reason: The same fine-tuning recipe leaves ASR essentially unchanged (63→64, 85→80, 68→73, 67→68), and refusal sometimes rises (10.8→15.8, 8.6→11.7). Harmful fine-tuning did not remove refusal for this model (R17–R24).
relationships.display_finding: Across run types ASR barely moved (63→64, 85→80, 68→73, 67→68), and refusal sometimes rose (10.8→15.8, 8.6→11.7), so the fine-tuning did not remove refusal for this model.

source_check.label: limits_scope
source_check.reason: DeepSeek has mixed, weak changes: small ASR increases in Baseline, CoT and ReAct, decreased ASR with Memory, and increased refusal in three run types. This heterogeneous group qualifies the claim; the small increases should not be described as established null effects.

relation.reason: The study directly measures changes in harmful compliance and refusal after toxic fine-tuning; harmful training is the intervention specified by V1.

tranche.reason: Fine-tuned versus non-fine-tuned models are compared under matched harassment-agent prompts, extending the harmful-fine-tuning question to multi-turn simulations.

source_check.notes: ASR measures conversations containing any harassment within 10 turns; RR measures refusal turns. Results concern explicitly prompted simulations. The supplied text is arXiv v3 dated 29 June 2026; its broad claim of consistent fine-tuning amplification overstates the DeepSeek results.
